title: Bend, solder, and route copper pipe
task: bending, soldering, and routing copper plumbing
setting: POV of a gloved plumber working from an outdoor concrete yard with a lever pipe bender and coiled red hose, then indoors among open tool cases and a gas torch, at a chased blue-plaster wall with copper stubs, across an opened floor cavity with joists and flux, and finally up in a loft among yellow insulation, rafters, and a second worker.

steps.text: Seat the copper tube in the lever bender and pull the bend
steps.detail: Gloved hands clamp a straight copper length in the circular former and haul the long black handle around until a finished bend lies on the concrete.
steps.expected: Action is acceptable as an early preparatory step provided the tube was first measured/marked and the correct former is used; bending un-marked tube risks incorrect geometry.

steps.text: Open the tool bags and pick torch, cutters, and flux brush
steps.detail: Inside beside wooden cabinets the worker rummages a white bag and a dirty hard case, lifts a torch on a yellow gas cylinder, grabs red pipe-slice wheels, and holds up a small flux brush.
steps.expected: Action is correct; gathering torch, cutters and flux brush is required before any joint preparation.

steps.text: Dry-fit elbows and stubs at the wall chase
steps.detail: At the blue plaster chase a vertical copper stub is pointed out, an elbow is offered onto a low run, and the upright pipe is left seated in the wall opening.
steps.expected: Dry-fitting stubs and elbows is correct only after cleaning and fluxing; dry-fit must also establish final level and alignment before any heat is applied.

steps.text: Heat each joint and feed solder into the fitting
steps.detail: The lit torch flame is played on wall and floor-level copper joints while the other hand brings solder wire to the hot cups until the metal wets.
steps.expected: Cleaning and fluxing must be completed BEFORE heating or feeding solder; soldering un-prepared joints is improper. Final leveling must already be locked in; soldering first is out of order.

steps.text: Span the two wall stubs with a spirit level and true them
steps.detail: A yellow spirit level is laid across the pair of protruding copper ends and adjusted until the vials read level.
steps.expected: Leveling and truing must occur during dry-fit BEFORE soldering; doing so after solder has set is out of order and requires reheating to correct.

steps.text: Assemble and solder the tee run in the floor cavity
steps.detail: Among open joists and rubble the torch reheats copper tees and elbows in the floor chase while short cut lengths are pushed into the fittings beside a flux pot.
steps.expected: Every tee, elbow and tube end in the cavity must be deburred, cleaned and fluxed before assembly; heating and soldering without those steps is incorrect.

steps.text: Carry copper up and lay out elbows in the loft
steps.detail: In the dark loft over yellow insulation the worker and a colleague pass long copper lengths across the joists and set loose elbows beside the run.
steps.expected: Staging long tube and loose elbows in the loft is acceptable once lower-level joints are complete and cooled; joint-preparation standards remain mandatory.

steps.text: Cut and feed the long copper length through the loft run
steps.detail: A cutter is worked on a loft pipe, then both workers push and guide a long straight copper tube forward under the rafters.
steps.expected: Cutting and feeding tube is correct provided the fresh cut is immediately deburred and cleaned before the end enters any fitting.

afterClip: Seat the remaining loft elbows, solder the overhead joints, and tie the new run back into the leveled wall stubs.
procedure: Plan route, measure runs and mark bend/cut positions on copper tube
Cut tube square to length with a rotary pipe cutter
Deburr every cut end inside and out
Clean pipe ends and fitting sockets to bright metal with abrasive or brush
Apply flux evenly to all joint surfaces
Bend tube on a lever bender with correct former size, following marks and avoiding kinks
Dry-assemble the full run, check alignment and level with a spirit level, adjust and mark final positions
Support and clip pipes securely in their permanent locations
Heat each fitting evenly with torch and feed solder until capillary fill is complete
Allow joints to cool undisturbed then wipe away excess flux
Route, cut, clean, flux, assemble and solder remaining sections through floors, walls and loft identically
Pressure-test the finished system for leaks
